title: standardize-ci-secret-caching-and-init-sequence
author: Aisha Raman
description: Motivation: CI workflows were intermittently failing and slow due to duplicated secret fetches and repeated environment bootstrap across workflows. This PR centralizes secret acquisition and common env initialization into a small, audited composite action and introduces a dedicated `init` job that runs early in the matrix to populate ephemeral caches. Goals: reduce flakiness, reduce token/secrets API calls, shorten average CI runtime for top-level jobs, and make secret usage auditable.
release_notes: Introduce a new composite action (actions/init-secret-cache) to standardize secret fetches and environment bootstrap in CI; add `ci:init` job to front-load cache & init, reduce duplicate secret API calls; update README/CONTRIBUTING with CI expectations.

notes_for_ops: After rollout, monitor CI average runtime on main for 48h. Look at actions/init-secret-cache invocation count and secret-service API metrics for unexpected spikes.
testing_performed: Local smoke runs + ephemeral-runner experiments across python and typescript matrices. Measured median job runtime reduction and validated that no secret material is persisted to workspace. Security scan run post-fix.
docs_changed: docs/ci.md and .github/CONTRIBUTING.md updated to document the init job and composite action usage for contributors.
additional_context: This PR is part of an effort (ENG-3210) to reduce CI costs and flakiness ahead of major release automation work. The composite action is intentionally small and isolated so it can be audited independently and reused by other repos in the organization.
